explain.say: In 1865 James Clerk Maxwell gathered everything known about electricity and magnetism into one theory, and out fell a prediction: light is an electromagnetic wave. Today we write his theory as four laws, sorted into four groups on the board. Let's meet them one at a time, in plain words.

explain.say: First, Gauss's law for electricity: electric charges make electric fields, and the field lines start on positive charges and end on negative ones. The total flux out of any closed surface equals the charge inside, over epsilon nought. You met this with the charged shell. So what makes an electric field in this law?

explain.say: Charges. Second, Gauss's law for magnetism: there are no magnetic charges, no lone north or south poles. Cut a bar magnet in half and you get two smaller magnets, each with both poles. So magnetic field lines always close into loops, and the net magnetic flux out of any closed surface is zero. What happens if you snap a magnet in two?

explain.say: Two complete magnets. Third, Faraday's law: a changing magnetic field makes an electric field that curls around it. That is the EMF in every generator and transformer. Fourth, Ampère's law with Maxwell's addition: currents make magnetic fields, and so does a changing electric field, even in empty space. Which of these two laws makes a power station work?

explain.say: Faraday's. Now the wow. Put the last two together: a changing electric field makes a magnetic field, which changes and makes an electric field, and so on, a wave that carries itself through empty space. Its speed is 1 over the square root of mu nought times epsilon nought: 300 thousand kilometres per second, the speed of light! Fantastic. Every radio, phone and sunbeam obeys these four laws.

faq.a: Four laws that describe all classical electricity and magnetism: Gauss's law for electric fields, Gauss's law for magnetic fields, Faraday's law of induction and the Ampère–Maxwell law.

faq.q: What does Gauss's law for magnetism mean?
faq.a: There are no isolated magnetic poles, so magnetic field lines always form closed loops. The net magnetic flux out of any closed surface is zero.
asks: Why are there no magnetic monopoles?

faq.q: What did Maxwell add to Ampère's law?
faq.a: He added the displacement current term: a changing electric field produces a magnetic field, just as a current does. Without it, electromagnetic waves would be impossible.

faq.q: How do Maxwell's equations predict light?
faq.a: Combining Faraday's law and the Ampère–Maxwell law gives a wave equation whose speed is 1 over root mu nought epsilon nought, about 3 times 10 to the 8 metres per second, which matched the measured speed of light.
asks: Why is light an electromagnetic wave?

faq.q: What does Faraday's law say in Maxwell's form?
faq.a: A changing magnetic flux creates an electric field that circulates around it. The circulation of E round a loop equals minus the rate of change of magnetic flux through it.

facts: James Clerk Maxwell published A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field in 1865.
Oliver Heaviside recast Maxwell's equations into the four compact vector equations used today.
One over the square root of mu nought times epsilon nought is about 3 times 10 to the 8 metres per second.

quiz.say: Which of Maxwell's equations says there are no magnetic monopoles?
quiz.show: Which of Maxwell's equations says there are no magnetic monopoles?
quiz.why: It says the net magnetic flux out of any closed surface is zero, so there are no lone poles.

wrong.1: Faraday's law links changing magnetic flux to electric fields.
wrong.2: The Ampère–Maxwell law says what produces magnetic fields, not that poles come in pairs.

quiz.say: With mu nought equal to 4 pi times 10 to the minus 7, and epsilon nought equal to 8.85 times 10 to the minus 12, what is 1 over the square root of their product?
quiz.show: With μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹², what is 1/√(μ₀ε₀)?

options.say: 3 times 10 to the 8 metres per second
3 times 10 to the 6 metres per second
9 times 10 to the 16 metres per second

quiz.why: The product is about 1.11 times 10 to the minus 17; its square root is 3.34 times 10 to the minus 9, and 1 over that is 3 times 10 to the 8 metres per second.

wrong.1: That slips two powers of ten in the square root.
wrong.2: That is c squared; you still need the square root.
